ideologies.name: Totalitarian Socialist
ideologies.description: Socialism as total mobilisation: one party, one doctrine and one leadership reach into every corner of life, and the security organs make sure that nothing is left outside the plan.

types.name: Maoism
types.description: Revolution made by the countryside against the city and kept alive by permanent mobilisation. The masses are the party's raw material, and no victory is ever declared final.

types.name: Stalinism
types.description: Identifying as a form of government applying and developing Marxist-Leninist policies, Stalinism emphasizes rapid industrialization and collectivization as well as the need for a strong, authoritative socialist state to purge any counter-revolutionary elements.

types.name: Chekist Communism
types.description: The security service does not serve the party; it has become the party. Socialism is whatever the organs need it to be in order to keep watching.

types.name: Jacobinism
types.description: Virtue enforced by the committee. The republic of equals is defended against its enemies with emergency powers that never quite expire.

types.name: Transhumanist-anarcho-primitivism
types.description: Abolish civilisation, keep the upgrades. A doctrine that wants the forest back and the human body rebuilt to survive in it, and sees no contradiction between the two.

types.name: Juche
types.description: Self-reliance raised to a state religion: one leader, one line, and a nation organised as a single fortress that owes nothing to anybody.

types.name: Pol Pot Thought
types.description: Year Zero. Cities are emptied, money is abolished and the past is declared closed, in the name of a peasant utopia that only the Organisation can see.

ideologies.name: Authoritarian Socialist
ideologies.description: State socialism in its managerial form: a single party holds every lever of the state, the market is tolerated as long as it stays useful, and the revolution is declared finished. Order and continuity come before doctrine.

types.name: Sovietism
types.description: Government by the councils, in name at least. Power flows upward through a pyramid of soviets that ratifies what the party has already decided.

types.name: Authoritarian Communism
types.description: The party owns the state and the state owns everything else. Communism administered from the top down, where discipline is the doctrine and dissent is a management problem.

types.name: Workerism
types.description: Politics begins and ends at the factory gate. The party exists to serve the shop floor, and anyone who has never worked a shift has no business speaking for those who have.

types.name: Transhumanist
types.description: The workers' state as an engineering project: technology is expected to finish the job that politics started, and the human being is one more system to be improved.

types.name: Socialist Military Junta
types.description: The officers have seized power in the name of the workers and intend to keep it on their behalf. Barracks discipline is presented as the shortest road to socialism.

types.name: Left Nationalism
types.description: Socialism inside one nation and for it: the class struggle is fought first of all against foreign capital, and the flag flies over the red banner.

types.name: Market Socialism
types.description: Public ownership of the commanding heights, private competition everywhere else. The plan sets the direction, the market sets the prices.

types.name: Xi Jinping Thought
types.description: Socialism with national characteristics for a new era: a disciplined party, a managed economy and a state that claims its place at the centre of the world.

types.name: Deutsche Communism
types.description: The German road to socialism, built on heavy industry, a vast security apparatus and the conviction that the workers' state must never be left unguarded.

types.name: Deutsche Conservatorist Socialism
types.description: Socialism kept as an institution rather than a promise: the workers' state is preserved the way a nation preserves its church and its army, with discipline, order and a deep suspicion of anyone who wants to reform it.

types.name: Maximalism
types.description: No half measures and no coalitions: the maximum programme, at once, or nothing at all.

types.name: Anarcho-Primitivism
types.description: Industrial civilisation is the problem, not the means. Dismantle the machine and let people live at a human scale again.

types.name: Populist Socialism
types.description: Socialism run from the rally, not the politburo. The line comes from whoever the crowd is still listening to this month, and the party apparatus exists to keep up with them.

ideologies.name: Vanguard Socialist
ideologies.description: The revolution led by a disciplined party of professional militants. Power belongs to the workers' councils, the strategy to the party, and the horizon is the world rather than the nation.

types.name: Leninist Internationalism
types.description: The party as the general staff of the working class, built by patient work in the factories and bound to a single strategy. The revolution is international or it is nothing.

types.name: Left Communism
types.description: Against parliaments, unions and national fronts alike: the class emancipates itself through its own councils, or it merely changes masters.

types.name: Neo-Sovietism
types.description: The Union was a mistake only in the way it ended. A new generation wants the councils, the planning and the red flag back, this time with servers instead of typewriters.

types.name: Communism
types.description: The classless society, reached through a party that leads the workers to it. Property is held in common, the economy is planned, and the state is expected to wither away once its work is done.

types.name: Marxism
types.description: History as the struggle between classes, and capital as the machine that drives it. The party reads the world through Marx and organises the workers to take the means of production.

types.name: Scientific Socialism
types.description: Socialism as a method rather than a hope. The laws of history are studied, the economy is modelled and planned, and the party answers to the data before it answers to sentiment.

ideologies.name: Revolutionary Socialist
ideologies.description: Capitalism is to be overthrown, not managed. A family of movements, from Trotskyists to syndicalists and anarchists, that agree on the uprising and on little else.

types.name: Trotskyism
types.description: Permanent revolution and workers' democracy, against both capital and the bureaucracy that claims to have replaced it. The revolution must spread, or it will rot.

types.name: Left Baathism
types.description: Arab unity, liberty and socialism, read from the left: land reform, nationalised oil and a single party that speaks in the name of the Arab masses.

types.name: Left Anarchist
types.description: No gods, no masters, no central committee. Federated communes and assemblies take the place of the state, which is not to be conquered but dismantled.

types.name: Nasserism
types.description: Arab socialism under a strong president: anti-imperialism, state-led industry and a single mass movement, with the army as guardian of the revolution.

types.name: Zapatismo
types.description: To lead by obeying. Indigenous communities govern themselves through assemblies and rotating councils, and ask of the state only that it stays away.

types.name: Socialism
types.description: Striving for equality and a socialist state by reformist means, democratic socialism aims to abolish or mitigate the effects of capitalism with public mandate.

ideologies.name: Reformist Socialist
ideologies.description: Socialism reached through elections, unions and legislation. The market is corrected and gradually outgrown, and the constitution is kept.

types.name: Progressivism
types.description: Reform as a habit of mind: expand rights, tax wealth, regulate the powerful, and trust that institutions can be made fairer one law at a time.

types.name: Reformist Socialism
types.description: Socialism by ballot and by statute. Capitalism is to be outgrown through nationalisations, strong unions and a welfare state, without anybody storming anything.

types.name: Social Democracy
types.description: A market economy tamed by collective bargaining, public services and progressive taxation. The class struggle is settled around a table, and everyone gets a pension.

types.name: Neo-Socialism
types.description: Planning, order and the nation in place of class war. A socialism that has lost patience with parliament and looks to a strong state and its technicians.

types.name: Syndicalism
types.description: The union is the school, the weapon and the future government of the working class. The general strike takes the economy, and the federations of producers run it.

types.name: Eurocommunism
types.description: Communists who accepted the ballot box. Free elections, civil liberties and a plural party system: a road to socialism that owes nothing to Moscow and everything to parliament.

ideologies.name: Liberal
ideologies.description: Civil liberties, pluralism and a market economy with a social conscience. Rights come first, and the state exists to guarantee them and to widen access to them.

types.name: Social Liberalism
types.description: Individual freedom needs more than the absence of the state: it needs schools, hospitals and a safety net. Civil rights and a regulated market, kept in careful balance.

types.name: Liberal Socialdemocrat
types.description: It is an ideology that blends individual self-determination with a strong, caring welfare state. The government intervenes in the market to actively diminish wealth and social inequalities. Equal opportunity is the result of public funding for education and national infrastructure. The ultimate goal is to see robust economic growth and social peace as mutually reinforcing goals.

types.name: Green Leftist
types.description: Climate and class are the same fight. Ecological transition, redistribution and grassroots democracy, pursued by parties that began as movements and still argue like them.

types.name: Left Populism
types.description: The people against the oligarchy. A charismatic movement that turns anger at the elites into a programme of redistribution, sovereignty and direct appeal to the squares.

types.name: Left Centrist
types.description: Moderate reformism for voters who distrust ideology: fiscal prudence with a social conscience, and an instinct for the coalition that offends the fewest.

ideologies.name: Centrist
ideologies.description: Centrism is a political position that rejects ideological extremes in an attempt to strike a balance between social justice and economic freedom. It supports pragmatism, compromise and gradual reform rather than radical change in order to preserve society’s stability. It combines progressive social values with regulated market economics in order to protect individual rights and democratic institutions.

types.name: Green Liberalism
types.description: Green liberalism is the use of market economic instruments in the service of strong environmental protection. It favors technological innovation and financial incentives over strict government bans and regulations. Use smart market signals such as carbon taxation to achieve ecological sustainability. From this perspective, environmental stewardship is a major opportunity for economic growth.

types.name: Ultra Liberalism
types.description: This philosophy prizes personal independence and economic freedom above all else. It calls for a major reduction in the role of government, in taxes and in welfare provision. Free market competition is seen as the most efficient regulator for society. This system substitutes state-backed collective safety nets with individual responsibility entirely.

types.name: Centrist Populism
types.description: This kind of politics claims to be the voice of reason for the reasonable majority. It sharply distances itself from the perceived dangers of both far-right and far-left extremes. Very pragmatic, direct and popular solutions are used to solve complex problems of the society. The movement mobilizes the broad mass of moderate citizens with an anti-elite rhetoric.

types.name: Neo-Liberalism
types.description: The market as the answer to almost every question. Privatisation, deregulation, open borders for capital and balanced budgets, with the state reduced to referee and enforcer of contracts.

types.name: Liberal Zionism
types.description: A Jewish state that is also a liberal democracy: equal rights for all its citizens, an independent judiciary and a negotiated settlement with the Palestinians, all within the Zionist project.

types.name: Techno-Zionism
types.description: The start-up nation as grand strategy. Cyber, defence technology and water engineering are the state's best exports and its best insurance, and the country is run like a laboratory.

ideologies.name: Conservative
ideologies.description: Institutions, property and gradual change. The free market and the constitutional order are defended as an inheritance to be handed on intact.

types.name: Conservatism
types.description: Considering rapid changes to society to be potentially harmful, conservatism espouses tradition and moderate reforms, sometimes advocating a return to old moral values.

types.name: Classical Liberalism
types.description: Limited government, free trade and the rule of law. The state should guard property and contracts, and otherwise keep out of the citizen's way.

types.name: Civic Nationalism
types.description: The nation as a community of citizens rather than of blood: shared institutions, a shared language of rights, and loyalty owed to the constitution above all.

types.name: Trumpism
types.description: America first, and the leader before the party. Tariffs, closed borders and open contempt for the establishment, held together by rallies and a permanent sense of grievance.

types.name: Americanism
types.description: The nation as a creed rather than a party programme: borders, industry and family put back at the centre, and a foreign policy that asks what is in it for America first.

types.name: Constitutionalist
types.description: The charter is the only sovereign. Powers are separated, mandates are limited, and every reform must first answer the question of whether it is permitted.

types.name: Christian Democracy
types.description: Social market economy, family and subsidiarity. A broad popular party that takes its ethics from the Church and its votes from the middle of society.

types.name: Classical Populism
types.description: The plain people against the politicians. No fixed doctrine, only a promise to lower taxes, cut privileges and say aloud what the voter says at home.

types.name: National Liberalism
types.description: Free markets at home and a firm flag abroad. Liberal in the economy, conservative on identity, and convinced that the nation-state is liberty's natural home.

types.name: Zionist Conservatism
types.description: The family, the synagogue and the army as the pillars of the Jewish state. Low taxes, a cautious government and tradition first, with security never put up for experiment.

types.name: National Liberal Zionism
types.description: Open markets and civil rights for citizens, a firm hand beyond the border. Liberal at home, nationalist abroad, and sure that the Jewish state is the guarantee of its own liberty.

ideologies.name: Reactionary
ideologies.description: A right that wants to restore rather than conserve: nation, religion and hierarchy against a liberal order it holds responsible for decline.

types.name: Military Democracy
types.description: This system is a cross between a democratic voting one and a general strong military leadership one. It places national security and strict discipline at the core of civic life. The right to participate in civic life is often contingent upon military service or loyalty to the ideals of national defense. It aims to uphold the democratic order through institutional strength, hierarchy and armed readiness.

types.name: Paleoconservatism
types.description: This ideology emphasizes local identity, traditional values, and tight restriction of government interference. It is strongly opposed to mass immigration, globalist economic treaties, and foreign military interventions. Religious traditions and the nuclear family are the ultimate bases of civil society. It supports economic protectionism to shield local workers and local cultures from global influences.

types.name: Traditionalismo
types.description: God, fatherland, ancient rights and the legitimate king. A counter-revolution that has been waiting, patiently and in arms, since the nineteenth century.

types.name: Clericalism
types.description: The Church as the conscience of the state, with a veto over its laws. Schools, marriage and public morals are handed back to those who claim to know best.

types.name: Corporatism
types.description: Society as a body, with each profession an organ. Employers and workers are bound into state-supervised corporations, so that class conflict has nowhere to happen.

types.name: Hardline Conservatism
types.description: Order, borders and identity, defended without apology. A right that keeps the ballot box but has stopped pretending to like the liberal consensus around it.

types.name: Paternalism
types.description: The state as a stern father: it provides, protects and decides. Citizens are cared for as long as they do not ask to be consulted.

types.name: Conservative Zionism
types.description: Security first, and the whole Land of Israel: a strong army, free enterprise and a national identity rooted in tradition, with little faith in concessions.

types.name: Red Army
types.description: The army that won the civil war has not handed the state back. Commanders and commissars govern in the name of the revolution, by order of the day.

ideologies.name: Authoritarian
ideologies.description: Power concentrated in an executive that tolerates elections and courts only as long as they do not get in the way. Stability is the stated aim, and the opposition is managed rather than defeated.

types.name: Patriotic Socialism
types.description: Welfare for the nation, discipline for its critics. A ruling movement that mixes social spending with flags, and treats opposition as a foreign import.

types.name: Illiberal Democracy
types.description: Elections are held and regularly won. In between, courts, media and universities are brought into line, so that the next result is never in much doubt.

types.name: Oligarchy
types.description: A handful of families and fortunes share out the state between them. Governments change; the owners of the ports, the banks and the television do not.

types.name: Technocracy
types.description: Government by those who know. Engineers and economists run the country as a problem to be optimised, and consider politics the main source of error.

types.name: Guided Democracy
types.description: The people vote, but within limits drawn by a guide who knows where the nation should go. Consensus is organised from above and then solemnly consulted.

types.name: Autocratic Liberalism
types.description: Open markets under a closed political system. Investors enjoy every guarantee that voters are denied, and growth is offered in place of consent.

ideologies.name: Autocratic
ideologies.description: Rule by one man, one clique or one army, without any real limit. Institutions survive as scenery.

types.name: Putinism
types.description: A vertical of power resting on the security services, the state companies and a restored sense of national greatness. Stability is the promise, and loyalty the only real institution.

types.name: Securocracy
types.description: The country is run by its intelligence chiefs and interior ministers. Every question is a security question, and every answer is classified.

types.name: Military Dictatorship
types.description: A general rules in his own name, with the army as his party. The constitution is suspended until further notice, and notice is never given.

types.name: Personalist Dictatorship
types.description: The state is one man, his relatives and his portrait. Institutions exist to carry out his will, and to be blamed when it fails.

types.name: Theocratic Dictatorship
types.description: A single ruler governs with the sanction of the clergy. Dissent is at once a crime and a sin, which saves the courts some time.

types.name: Technocratic Dictatorship
types.description: An unelected cabinet of experts with emergency powers. The plan is rational, the figures add up, and nobody was asked.

types.name: Corporatocracy
types.description: The largest companies no longer lobby the government: they are the government. Policy is decided in boardrooms and announced like a quarterly result.

types.name: Mafia State
types.description: Organised crime and public office have merged into a single structure. Contracts, courts and police are run as a protection racket with a flag.

types.name: Military Junta
types.description: A council of officers holds power collectively after the coup. Army, navy and air force each take their share, and call the arrangement national salvation.

types.name: People's Liberation Army
types.description: The gun commands the party. The armed forces rule directly, combining a Marxist vocabulary with the habits of a general staff.

types.name: US Army
types.description: The Joint Chiefs have assumed the powers of a paralysed republic. The constitution is said to be merely suspended, pending a return to normality.

types.name: Personal Dictatorship
types.description: One ruler, and no ideology worth the name. Power is kept through patronage, fear and a talent for outliving every rival.

types.name: Soviet Army
types.description: Marshals in place of secretaries. The armed forces have taken over a socialist state in order to save it from its own politicians.

types.name: Theocratic Autocracy
types.description: Supreme authority belongs to a religious leader who answers to God alone. The clergy staff the state, and scripture serves as its constitution.

types.name: Kleptocracy
types.description: The state exists to be looted by those who run it. Offices are investments, the budget is the return, and elections are a business expense.

types.name: Zionist Stratocracy
types.description: The army is the state. A security cabinet of generals governs in the name of survival, and civilian politics lasts only as far as the General Staff allows.

ideologies.name: Absolutist
ideologies.description: Sovereignty rests in a crown, by inheritance or by divine right. The dynasty is the state, and politics is what happens at court.

types.name: Monarchism
types.description: The crown as the living symbol of the nation and the guarantee of its continuity. A king above the parties and, ideally, above the quarrel.

types.name: Casa Savoia
types.description: The House of Savoy returns to the Quirinal. The dynasty that united Italy offers itself once more as the one institution older than the country's divisions.

types.name: Absolute Monarchy
types.description: The sovereign reigns and governs. Ministers serve at his pleasure, the law is his decree, and the dynasty is the only constitution.

types.name: Divine Monarchy
types.description: The ruler holds the throne by the will of heaven and is himself an object of reverence. To question him is not politics but blasphemy.

types.name: Imperial Autocracy
types.description: One emperor over many peoples, ruling by decree through governors and guards. The empire is its own justification.

types.name: Oligarchic Monarchy
types.description: A king reigns, but a circle of great families and princes divides the offices and the revenue. The throne is the seal on their agreement.

types.name: Theocratic Monarchy
types.description: Crown and altar in one person. The monarch is both sovereign and guardian of the faith, and governs with the clergy as his natural ministers.

types.name: Monarcho-Zionism
types.description: A crowned head for the Jewish state. A king in Jerusalem stands above the parties and the courts, and the Zionist project takes the form of a single dynasty.

ideologies.name: Ultranationalist
ideologies.description: The nation as the supreme value, above law, class and individual. A single party and a single leader claim to embody it, and treat everything foreign as a threat.

types.name: Neo-Fascist
types.description: The heirs of the regime in new suits. Nation, order and the strong state, with the nostalgia kept just deniable enough for television.

types.name: Neo-Nazist
types.description: Racial doctrine and the cult of violence, handed down by a movement that lost a world war and learned nothing from it.

types.name: Fascist
types.description: Everything within the state, nothing outside it. One leader, one party and a nation mobilised like an army, for which war is the natural condition.

types.name: NationalSocialist
types.description: The national community defined by blood and led by a single will. Expansion abroad and persecution at home are the same policy.

types.name: Nazi Maoism
types.description: People's war for the fatherland. A fringe doctrine that borrows the methods of the far left to serve the myths of the far right.

types.name: Strassarite
types.description: The second revolution that never came: a nationalism that calls itself anti-capitalist, and wants industry nationalised and the nation purified at the same time.

types.name: National Bolshevism
types.description: Red flag, national soil. The planned economy and the strong state of the Soviets, put at the service of the nation instead of the class.

types.name: National Syndicalism
types.description: The unions absorbed into the nation. Workers and owners are organised in vertical syndicates under a single party, and a strike becomes treason.

types.name: Ultranationalist Socialism
types.description: Social justice for the nation's own, and for nobody else. Welfare, land and work are promised to the people and denied to everyone outside it.

types.name: Ultranationalism
types.description: The nation above every law, treaty and neighbour. Its greatness is the only programme, and its enemies are everywhere.

types.name: Kahanism
types.description: A religious ultranationalism that wants a state governed by religious law and emptied of those it considers foreign to it.

ideologies.name: Fundamentalist
ideologies.description: The state as an instrument of the faith. Religious law overrides civil law, and the clergy or their militants claim the last word.

types.name: Islamic Fundamentalism
types.description: The sharia as the whole of the law. The state exists to enforce the faith as its scholars read it, and politics is a branch of jurisprudence.

types.name: Christian Fundamentalism
types.description: Scripture as statute. The nation is to be governed by biblical morality, and secular institutions are treated as a mission field.

types.name: Clerical Fascism
types.description: The party's uniform under the priest's blessing. Authoritarian nationalism presents itself as the armed defence of the Church.

types.name: Religious Nationalism
types.description: Faith and nation are one identity. To belong to the people is to belong to its religion, and minorities are guests at best.

types.name: Ultratraditionalism
types.description: The modern world is the error. Every reform since some lost golden age is to be undone, and ancestral custom restored as law.

types.name: Theocratic State
types.description: The clergy govern directly. Councils of jurists and priests hold the final word over parliament, courts and army alike.

types.name: Jihadism
types.description: Armed struggle as a religious duty without borders. The movement fights to build its state on conquered ground, and recognises no other.

types.name: Evangelical Nationalism
types.description: The country has a covenant, and the congregations intend to hold it to it. Megachurches, broadcasters and voters move as a single bloc.

types.name: Hindu Nationalism
types.description: Hindutva: the nation defined as a Hindu civilisation. A mass movement of cadres and temples that wants the state to reflect the faith of the majority.

types.name: Bibism
types.description: The devotion and the system of power that grew around the Israeli prime minister, known by his nickname 'Bibi'. Coalition partners, party and state institutions orbit one leader, and his political survival becomes the purpose of the government.

types.name: Religious Zionism
types.description: The settlement of the whole Land of Israel as a religious duty. The state is the beginning of redemption, the rabbis its guides and Halakha the measure of its laws.
